co_iron_curtain.blurb: Iron Curtain is a south-facing wall high on Sheep Mountain in the Narrows stretch of Poudre Canyon, west of Fort Collins, directly above the Dihedrals. It holds about a dozen lines, nearly all of them bolted sport climbs, with a single trad route. Grades run from 5.9 up to 5.12, and most routes fall in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, so it suits climbers already comfortable on steeper ground. The left side is a set of overhanging roofs, the middle turns to technical slab broken by a mid-height roof band, and a distinct block caps the triangular main face. Routes are short, around 80 feet. Loose blocks sit on the lower ledges, so watch your footing.

co_nancy_s_rock.blurb: Nancy's Rock is a small single-pitch slab on Palisade Mountain, on the Big Thompson Canyon side of the Estes Park Valley between Loveland and Estes Park. The eleven routes are a mix of bolted lines and gear-protected climbs, mostly 5.6 to 5.10 with one 5.11, so it works well for newer leaders and for climbers wanting an easy warm-up. Routes are roughly 55 to 65 feet and share an anchor at the top, which also makes top-roping straightforward. A couple of very short climbs sit above the main face. The base is a short uphill walk from the road. Watch for poison ivy at the left end of the wall and for wasps on the face.
